auth_state_reconstruction.manus_rule: Authentication state is a subfield of the address, not part of it. Older images were taken signed in, because MANUS did not yet know how to screenshot in incognito. Transcripts with no image were taken incognito. More recent images were taken signed out, and show it in the frame. Find the oldest image showing signed out; from there on, authentication state is incognito.
auth_state_reconstruction.threshold_evidence: Determined empirically, not assumed. A colour-signature detector for the Google 'Sign in' pill (blue-excess against a dark header, calibrated on three known cases: a signed-out capture, a signed-in capture and an incognito capture) was run over all 197 imaged captures. Detections cluster tightly at 0.042-0.046 from 2026-08-04 onward and are absent before. The earliest is 20260804-mindcontrolpoems-blog-signedout, whose legacy slug and sf line independently record 'signed out'. Both boundary images were then inspected visually: the 4 August frame shows the 'Sign in' pill plainly; the 3 August frame does not.
auth_state_reconstruction.limitation: The indicator is only visible where the screenshot includes the Google page header. Many captures are cropped panels or scrolled past it, so absence of the indicator is NOT evidence of being signed in. For those, the state is carried from the threshold rule and the record says so. Every observation records whether the indicator was directly visible.
